Read /tmp/claude-501/trail-brief.md for repo context and sandbox notes; its trail rules do not apply except: TDD with mutants, checks by exit code, no session links in commits, never merge/force-push. Branch `fix/output-bound` from `origin/refactor/compose-outcomes` (the head of the core chain, PR #126); open a draft PR with base `refactor/compose-outcomes`: `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1 gh pr create --draft --base refactor/compose-outcomes --head fix/output-bound --title ... --body ... < /dev/null` (plain `gh pr create` hangs). git network and cargo need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`.
Finding (independent review of #121, HIGH): the NAPI 16 MiB cumulative cap is meant to bound OUTPUT (comment at `crates/michi-core/src/napi/input.rs` ~:33-45 and spec 04 ~:202 assume each held byte is written at most 19 times). That is false: the `truncated[N]{section,row,field,removed}` table (`toon/table.rs` ~:98-104, `push_truncated`) writes the FIELD NAME again for every cut cell, and the field name is charged once. Measured in Node with a 4 KiB control-character field name and 1,000 rows of 201-character cells: ~261 KB held rendered to 95x in text and 112x in JSON. At 60,000 rows the input stayed under the cap, yet `renderText()` failed with "Failed to convert rust `String` into napi `string`": exactly what #121 says can no longer happen.
Do: (1) reproduce it as a failing test (Rust-level amplification test over the NAPI accounting plus a Node test in `packages/michi-node`), (2) make the bound TRUE for every output surface and every composed section kind: derive the worst-case output factor from the actual writers, and charge what each held item can cost in output (for example a field name once per cell/row it can be repeated in, key/section names wherever they are repeated) or add an exact output-size guard that fails with a clear error before the oversize string is built; prefer accounting in `napi/` (do not change rendered output; `toon/table.rs`, `response.rs`, `section.rs` are being edited by another trail: do not touch them, a call-site fix aside), (3) a test that computes the real amplification over a hostile matrix (control characters, long names, many rows, truncated cells, partial-success and status rows, error causes) and asserts held-bytes x documented factor >= output, run in debug and measured in Node at the cap, (4) correct the doc comments and spec 04 with the real factor and how it is enforced. Mutants: lower the factor, skip the field-name charge: each must fail a test. Checks: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, the doctests as CI runs them (see ci.yml; `just test-rust` does not run doctests), `just typos`, `just check`, `pnpm build && pnpm test` in packages/michi-node. Changeset if JS-visible limits change. Final message <= 150 words.

# Shared brief: michi hardening trails (read fully)

Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/michi (Rust workspace; `michi-core` FSL, `michi-graph` MIT no_std, `michi-pipeline` async, NAPI shim in `packages/michi-node`, its exports in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`). 0.10.0 is released; we are pre-1.0 and every consumer is our own repo, so **breaking changes are fine and legacy surface is removed, never shimmed**. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `PRINCIPLES.md`; ADRs and `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` record decisions you must not re-litigate (read headings first).
Four read-only audits produced the findings you act on: `/tmp/claude-501/audit-{architecture,security,rust-perf,duplication}.md`. Your trail names the finding numbers; read those entries (evidence, proposed change, "Not examined") and verify each is still true on current main before changing code. If a finding is wrong or already fixed, say so and skip it.

## Parallel trails, strict ownership (this is how we avoid conflicts)
Other trails run at the same time in other worktrees. Edit only files your trail owns. If your change forces a one-line call-site fix in a file another trail owns (for example `napi.rs`), make the minimal fix and say so in your report. Never reformat or reorganize files you do not own. If `git merge origin/main` brings conflicts in your files, resolve them keeping both sides' intent.
Trails: T1 envelope integrity (core model files, toon/ writers); T2 NAPI structure (`napi.rs` and `packages/michi-node`); T3 release-signing CI (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `.prototools`); T4 pipeline error redaction (`crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs`, `redact.rs`, `fuzz/`, trust-model docs); T5 docs/tests/CI hygiene (docs drift, new tests, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); T6 pipeline observers.

## Flow (autonomous; never ask questions; decide and report the decision)
1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (git network and cargo need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command; use `$TMPDIR` for temp files; keep commands simple, no computed git arguments).
2. TDD: a failing test first, confirm it fails for the right reason, then fix. For every behavioral claim, break the code on purpose (mutant), watch the test fail, revert. Report the mutants.
3. Update docs/spec for anything you change (CI's "Spec first" job) and rustdoc for every pub item. Add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` for code changes (look at existing ones and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; package `michi-core` unless your change is elsewhere; start a paragraph with `Breaking:` when behavior or API breaks). No changeset for CI-only or docs-only changes.
4. Checks, judged by exit code only: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, plus `just check` once at the end, plus anything specific to your trail (Node: `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`; workflows: `actionlint` and `just zizmor`).
5. Commit (conventional, why-not-what; **no claude.ai session links, no Claude-Session trailer**), push, open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, how checked, what was not run, any decision you made). Never merge, never force-push, never push to main.

## Final message (<= 200 words)
PR URL; per-finding outcome (fixed / skipped with reason); decisions you made; checks with exit codes; mutants run; anything left or surprising.

696:mod tests {
# Default recipe: run full CI pipeline via moon & just
default: ci

# ── Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
    moon run :build

build-release:
    cargo build --release --workspace

build-node:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform

build-node-release:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform --release

# ── Test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
    moon run :test

test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace

test-rust-all:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features

# Each published crate alone with its default features: a workspace-wide run unifies features across crates.
test-crates-default:
    cargo nextest run -p michi-core
    cargo nextest run -p michi-graph
    cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline

# The fixed group's semver release type from pending changesets (front matter only).
pending-release-type:
    python3 scripts/pending-release-type.py "$(grep -m1 '^version' crates/michi-core/Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')"

# michi-graph is MIT: fail if a non-permissive license enters its normal or build dependencies.
check-graph-license:
    python3 scripts/test_check_permissive_deps.py
    cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features | python3 scripts/check-permissive-deps.py michi-graph

# Post-release check: install a *published* version from npm and crates.io into clean projects and use it.
# Needs network. `SMOKE_RETRY_SECONDS` (default 600) bounds the wait for the registries.
smoke-published version:
    scripts/smoke-published.sh {{version}}

test-rust-release:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --release

test-node: build-node
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm test

# ── Lint & Format ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check: fmt-check clippy doc-check fuzz-check zizmor deny typos fmt-md-check

# Static security audit of the workflows (needs zizmor 1.29.0, the version CI runs).
zizmor:
